definition_en: a greeting used when meeting someone or answering the phone
core_image: 一个人推开门，抬手向屋里的人打招呼
scene: 他推开门，抬手向屋里的人打招呼。She said hello to the new pupil.

senses.title: A word used when meeting someone
senses.definition: a greeting used when meeting someone or starting a conversation
senses.definitionCN: 见面或开口交谈时用的招呼语
senses.example: She said hello to the new pupil.
senses.why: Hello spread in the nineteenth century as a spoken greeting, probably from the older call hallo, and it opens a meeting between people.
senses.whyCN: hello 在十九世纪作为口头招呼语流行开来，可能来自更早的 hallo「喂」，用来开启两个人的会面。

senses.title: A call to see if anyone is there
senses.definition: a call used to attract attention or check that someone is present
senses.definitionCN: 用来引起注意，或确认有没有人在
senses.example: Hello, is anyone there?
senses.why: When the other person cannot be seen, as on a telephone, the same word is used to send a voice out and test for a reply.
senses.whyCN: 看不见对方时，比如在电话里，就用同一个词把声音送出去，试探有没有回应。

senses.title: A greeting as a countable thing
senses.definition: an act or instance of greeting someone
senses.definitionCN: 一次打招呼的行为
senses.example: She gave me a warm hello at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 她在门口热情地跟我打招呼。
senses.why: Once the spoken word is treated as an event, it becomes a noun, so one hello is one act of greeting.
senses.whyCN: 口头的话一旦被当作一件事，就成了名词，所以 one hello 就是一次打招呼。

senses.title: An informal word for hello
senses.definition: a short, informal greeting used among people who know each other
senses.definitionCN: 熟人之间随口使用的简短招呼
senses.example: She waved and said hi.
senses.why: Hi is a clipped, casual form of hello, and its short sound suits a quick greeting between people already acquainted.
senses.whyCN: hi 是 hello 的口语缩短形式，短促的声音正适合熟人之间快速打个招呼。

senses.title: A call to attract someone's attention
senses.definition: a call used to stop a stranger or get their attention
senses.definitionCN: 叫住陌生人或让对方注意自己时用的声音
senses.example: Hi, you dropped your glove!
senses.why: The same short call that greets a friend can also stop a stranger in the street, so hi works as a way of catching someone's ear.
senses.whyCN: 同一个短促的招呼既能问候朋友，也能在街上叫住陌生人，所以 hi 也用来抓住别人的耳朵。

definition_en: the place where you live, or to the place where you belong
core_image: 一扇亮着灯的窗，窗内桌上摆着热饭和两把椅子
scene: 夜里那扇窗还亮着灯，桌上摆着热饭和两把椅子。She went home after work.

senses.title: The place where a person lives
senses.definition: the place where someone lives, especially with family
senses.definitionCN: 人居住的地方，尤指与家人同住之处
senses.example: She went home after work.
senses.why: Home goes back to Old English hām, 'dwelling, village', related to German Heim, and names the place a person settles in.
senses.whyCN: home 来自古英语 hām「住处、村落」，与德语 Heim 同源，指人安顿下来的地方。

senses.title: Family life and the feeling of belonging
senses.definition: the family life and warmth that a dwelling holds
senses.definitionCN: 一个住所里承载的家庭生活与温暖
senses.example: They made a happy home together.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一起营造了一个快乐的家。
senses.why: A house becomes a home when people live in it together, so the word also names the family life inside it.
senses.whyCN: 有人一起生活，房子才成为家，所以这个词也指里面的家庭生活。

senses.title: The place or country one comes from
senses.definition: the town or country where one was born or grew up
senses.definitionCN: 出生或长大的城镇、国家
senses.example: He left home at eighteen.
senses.why: The place one grew up in is the first home, so the word extends from a single dwelling to a whole hometown or country.
senses.whyCN: 人长大的地方是第一个家，于是这个词从一所住宅扩展到整个家乡或故国。

senses.title: A place where people are cared for
senses.definition: an institution where people in need of care live
senses.definitionCN: 供需要照料的人长期居住的机构
senses.example: The old man moved into a home for the elderly.
senses.why: An institution that gives people a place to live and care is also called a home, because living there replaces the family house.
senses.whyCN: 给人住处和照料的机构也叫 home，因为住在那里替代了自家的房子。

definition_en: having a high temperature, spicy, or very popular

pos.zh: 形容词：热的、辣的、热门的、激烈的

senses.title: Having a high temperature
senses.definition: having a high temperature, enough to burn or warm
senses.definitionCN: 温度高到会烫人或取暖
senses.example: The soup is too hot to drink.
senses.why: Hot goes back to Old English hāt, related to German heiß, and names what has a high degree of heat.
senses.whyCN: hot 来自古英语 hāt，与德语 heiß 同源，指热度很高。

senses.title: Strongly spiced and burning in the mouth
senses.definition: strongly spiced, producing a burning feeling in the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 香料多、入口有灼烧感
senses.example: This curry is very hot.
senses.why: Chilli makes the tongue feel as if it were burning, so the heat word also describes spicy food.
senses.whyCN: 辣椒让舌头像被烧着一样，于是这个表示「热」的词也用来形容辣。

senses.title: Popular and in great demand
senses.definition: very popular and in great demand at the moment
senses.definitionCN: 当下很受欢迎、人人争着要
senses.example: This song is hot right now.
senses.why: Something in demand is like food just off the stove, still hot, so the heat word came to mean sought after.
senses.whyCN: 抢手的东西就像刚离火的饭菜、还冒着热气，于是这个表示「热」的词引申为抢手。

senses.title: Intense or violent
senses.definition: full of strong feeling or activity
senses.definitionCN: 情绪或活动非常强烈
senses.example: They had a hot argument in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在院子里吵得很激烈。
senses.why: An argument heats up as feelings rise, so hot describes a conflict at its most intense.
senses.whyCN: 争吵一起，情绪就升温，所以 hot 形容冲突最激烈的时候。

definition_en: a building where people live, or to provide a place for something

senses.title: A building that people live in

senses.definitionCN: 供人居住的建筑物
senses.example: They bought a house near the school.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在学校附近买了房子。
senses.why: House goes back to Old English hūs, related to German Haus, and names the building a family lives in.
senses.whyCN: house 来自古英语 hūs，与德语 Haus 同源，指一家人居住的建筑。

senses.title: A chamber of a parliament
senses.definition: one of the chambers of a parliament
senses.definitionCN: 议会中的一院
senses.example: The bill passed the upper house.
senses.exampleCN: 法案在上议院获得通过。
senses.why: A parliament meets in one great building and each chamber is called a house, so the building word became an institution's name.
senses.whyCN: 议会在一座大建筑里开会，每一院都被称作一个 house，于是这个建筑词成了机构的名字。

senses.title: The audience in a theatre
senses.definition: the audience filling a theatre, as in a full house
senses.definitionCN: 剧场里坐满的观众，如 a full house
senses.example: The show played to a full house.
senses.why: When every seat is taken, the whole theatre building is filled, so house came to mean the audience itself.
senses.whyCN: 座位全部坐满，整座剧场被填满，于是 house 转指观众本身。

senses.title: To provide a place to live or stay
senses.definition: to give someone or something a place to live or be kept
senses.definitionCN: 给某人某物提供住处或存放处
senses.example: The hall houses two hundred students.
senses.exampleCN: 这座大厅住着两百名学生。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, so to house people is to put them inside a building.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，house 一群人就是把这些人安置进一座建筑里。

senses.title: In what way
senses.definition: in what way or by what means
senses.definitionCN: 用什么方式、靠什么办法
senses.example: How did you find the way?
senses.why: How goes back to Old English hū, the instrumental form of the word for 'who or what', so it asks 'by what means'.

senses.title: To what degree
senses.definition: to what degree or extent
senses.definitionCN: 达到什么程度
senses.example: How tall is your brother?
senses.why: The same question word can measure an amount instead of a method, so how also asks about degree.
senses.whyCN: 同一个疑问词也能衡量数量而不是方法，所以 how 也问程度。

senses.title: In what condition, especially of health
senses.definition: in what condition, often asked about someone's health
senses.definitionCN: 处于什么状况，常用于问候健康
senses.example: How are you today?
senses.why: Asking how a person is asks about the state they are in, which is why the word became the standard health greeting.
senses.whyCN: 问一个人 how，就是问他处在什么状态，所以这个词成了问候健康的标准说法。

senses.title: Inside a space or container
senses.definition: within a space, container or area
senses.definitionCN: 处在某个空间、容器或区域内部
senses.example: The keys are in the drawer.
senses.why: In comes from Old English innan, 'within', related to the word for entering, so being inside something is its base.
senses.whyCN: in 来自古英语 innan「在里面」，与表示「进入」的词同源，处在某物内部是它的本义。

senses.title: During a period of time
senses.definition: during a period, or after a length of time
senses.definitionCN: 在某段时间之内，或过了若干时间之后
senses.example: We will meet in an hour.
senses.why: A stretch of time is treated like a container, with events placed inside it, which is how in also marks periods.
senses.whyCN: 一段时间被当成容器，事情被放进去，in 就是这样标记时间段的。

senses.title: Within a state, field or language
senses.definition: within a condition, activity or medium
senses.definitionCN: 处在某种状态、活动或媒介之中
senses.example: She spoke in French.
senses.why: States, languages and fields work like spaces you can stand inside, so in covers them as well.
senses.whyCN: 状态、语言和领域都像可以站进去的空间，所以 in 也覆盖这些用法。

senses.title: Fashionable or currently popular

senses.example: Short coats are in this winter.

senses.why: What is popular is inside the current fashion, so be in came to mean being in style.
senses.whyCN: 流行的东西正处在当下的风尚圈子里，所以 be in 表示正时髦。

senses.title: Joining a subject to who or what it is

senses.definitionCN: be 的第三人称单数形式，把主语与它的身份或性质连起来
senses.example: She is a teacher.
senses.why: Is is the third-person singular of be, and its oldest work is to join a subject to the name or quality that describes it.

senses.definitionCN: 用在 there is 中说明某物存在

senses.why: In there is, is joins nothing to a description; it simply states that the thing is there, which is be's other old duty.

definition_en: the thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
core_image: 一只小猫坐在窗台上，尾巴轻轻摆向一边
scene: 一只小猫坐在窗台上，尾巴轻轻摆向一边。It is a quiet little cat.
sceneCN: 这里 it 是「它」（第 01 个义项）；句意是它是一只安静的小猫。

pos.zh: 代词：它、这（指情况、天气、时间）

senses.title: The thing or animal already mentioned
senses.definition: the thing or animal already mentioned or easily identified
senses.definitionCN: 前面提到或容易指认的事物、动物
senses.example: It is a quiet little cat.
senses.why: It goes back to Old English hit, the neutral third-person pronoun, used for anything that is not a person.
senses.whyCN: it 来自古英语 hit，是中性的第三人称代词，用来指不是人的事物。

senses.title: The weather, time or situation
senses.definition: used for weather, time or a general situation
senses.definitionCN: 用来指天气、时间或笼统的处境
senses.example: It is raining outside.
senses.why: Weather and time have no named thing behind them, so English puts it in the subject place to hold the sentence together.
senses.whyCN: 天气和时间背后没有具体名词可指，英语就用 it 占住主语的位置，把句子撑起来。

senses.title: A placeholder before the real subject
senses.definition: used as an empty subject when the real content comes later
senses.definitionCN: 真正的内容放在后面时，用它占住主语位置
senses.example: It is hard to say.
senses.why: When the real subject is a long phrase placed at the end, a short it stands in front so the sentence can start.
senses.whyCN: 真正的主语是一长串放在句末的内容时，先用一个短的 it 站前面，句子才起得了头。

definition_en: to push yourself off the ground, or to rise suddenly
core_image: 一个人屈膝起跳，双脚离地，影子落在下方的地面
scene: 他从地面起跳，双脚离地，影子落在下方。The children jump over the rope.
sceneCN: 这里 jump 是「跳」（第 01 个义项）；句意是孩子们跳绳。

derivatives.zh: 由 jump 加 -er 构成，义为「跳跃者、毛衣」
由 jump 加 -ing 构成，义为「跳跃」
由 jump 加 -y 构成，义为「紧张不安的」

senses.title: To push off the ground into the air
senses.definition: to push off the ground so that both feet leave it
senses.definitionCN: 双脚蹬地离地弹起
senses.example: The children jump over the rope.
senses.why: The word's core action is pushing off the ground so that the body leaves it, which is a jump at its plainest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心动作是蹬地让身体离开地面，这就是最朴素的「跳」。

senses.title: To rise suddenly and sharply
senses.definition: to increase suddenly and by a large amount
senses.definitionCN: 突然大幅上升
senses.example: Prices jumped last month.
senses.why: A price can leap the way a body leaps: the sudden sharp rise is pictured as leaving the old level in one spring.
senses.whyCN: 价格能像身体一样起跳：突然的猛涨被想象成一跃离开原来的水平。

senses.title: To pass over others without waiting
senses.definition: to move past others or a stage without waiting one's turn
senses.definitionCN: 不按顺序、越过别人或某一环节
senses.example: He jumped the queue at the ticket office.
senses.why: To jump a queue is to leap over the people waiting, using the jump as a way of getting past them.
senses.whyCN: jump a queue 就是从排队的人头上跃过去，借「跳」越过他们。

senses.title: A spring off the ground, as a noun
senses.definition: one act of springing off the ground
senses.definitionCN: 一次离地弹起的动作
senses.example: She won the long jump at school.
senses.why: The verb turned into a noun, so a jump counts one spring or one event built on jumping.
senses.whyCN: 动词转作名词，a jump 就是数一次弹跳，或一项以跳为基础的项目。
